rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is addressed specifically to the Jews, not to other peoples before or after them.
rows.anchor: أي اليهود خاصة لا على من عداهم من الأولين والآخرين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جرير وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: They explain an animal with an undivided hoof or claw, such as camels, ostriches, geese, and ducks.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس وابن جرير وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd restricts the referent to camels.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن زيد أنه الأبل فقط

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī includes all predators, dogs, cats, and animals that hunt with their claws.
rows.anchor: الجبائي : يدخل فيه كل السباع والكلاب

rows.speaker: القتبي والبلخي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybī and al-Balkhī mean clawed birds and hoofed beasts, using ‘nail’ figuratively for hoof; the Imam considers this unlikely.
rows.anchor: القتبي والبلخي أنه ذو المخلب من الطير وذو الحافر من الدواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generalization of the ban may itself be the punishment for wrongdoing, since some of these things were already prohibited.
rows.anchor: المسبب عن الظلم هو تعميم التحريم لأن البعض كان حراما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also allows reading the phrase as every clawed animal that was lawful, on the stated contextual indication.
rows.anchor: يراد كل ذي ظفر حلال بقرينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement confirms the earlier restriction of forbidden foods and refutes the Jews’ claim that the restrictions had applied since Noah and Abraham.
rows.anchor: تحقيق لما سلف من حصر المحرمات فيما فصل

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some scholars take the verse as completing the preceding argument: animal restrictions and rules about bahīra and sāʾiba were imposed on Jews specifically as punishment.
rows.anchor: المحققين : إن ذلك تتميم لما قبله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads ẓufur with ẓāʾ kasra and fāʾ sukūn.
rows.anchor: الحسن ( ظفر ) بكسر الظاء وسكون الفاء

rows.speaker: أبو السماك
rows.claim: Abū al-Sammāk reads both consonants with kasra.
rows.anchor: أبو السماك بكسرهما وقريء كما قال

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Another reading, cited by Abū al-Baqāʾ, has ẓāʾ ḍamma and fāʾ sukūn.
rows.anchor: قال أبو البقاء ظفر بضم الظاء وسكون الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibited fats do not include meat; they are thin fat on intestines and rumen and kidney fat, though a broader sense is also reported.
rows.anchor: لا لحومهما فانها باقية على الحل والمراد بالشحوم ما يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Of cattle and sheep’ attaches to the following ‘We prohibited’; naming the fats again adds connection and emphasis.
rows.anchor: ( من البقر ) متعلق بحرمنا بعده وكان يكفي حينئذ أن يقال

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also permits attaching ‘of cattle’ to ‘every clawed animal,’ meaning some cattle, with the prohibition clause explaining what is forbidden.
rows.anchor: أبو البقاء وظاهر صنيعه اختياره مع أنه خلاف الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception concerns fat attached to the animals’ backs; grammarians differ whether it is connected or disconnected from ‘fats.’
rows.anchor: ما علق بظهورهما والاستثناء منقطع أو متصل من الشحوم

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa treats the exception as disconnected: someone swearing not to eat fat breaks the oath only by eating abdominal fat.
rows.anchor: عنه لو حلف لا يأكل شحما سحنث بشحم البطن فقط

rows.speaker: صاحباه
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa’s companions say eating back fat also breaks that oath because it is fat and melts in fire, supporting a connected exception.
rows.anchor: صاحباه فقالا يحنث بشحم الظهر أيضا لأنه شحم

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam favors disconnection: back fat is meat in reality, cooked and eaten as meat, and its seller is a butcher; this outweighs the usual presumption for a connected exception.
rows.anchor: وللامام رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه لحم حقيقة لأنه ينشأ من الدم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهما
rows.claim: One explanation identifies al-ḥawāyā as the entrails or places where feces collect.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهما أو المرابض

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd explains al-ḥawāyā as the udder or places where milk gathers.
rows.anchor: كما روي عن ابن زيد أو المصارين

rows.speaker: غير واحد من أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Several lexicographers identify al-ḥawāyā as the intestines and bowels.
rows.anchor: المصارين والأمعاء كما قال غير واحد من أهل اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a connected exception, proponents supply ‘fats of the entrails’ or explain the word as the fat wrapped around them.
rows.anchor: للقائل بالاتصال أن يقول العطف على تقدير مضاف أي شحوم الحوايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other grammarians allow coordinating al-ḥawāyā with either ‘their backs’ or ‘their fats.’
rows.anchor: وجوز غير واحد أن يكون العطف على ( ظهورهما ) وأن يكون على ( شحومهما )

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: Some early authorities take what is attached to bone as tail fat adjoining the coccyx; another explanation is marrow, though it is not ordinarily called fat.
rows.anchor: بعض السلف وهو يعطف قوله تعالى : ( أو ما أختلط بعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥawāyā is variously analyzed as plural of ḥāwiya, ḥāwiyāʾ, or ḥawiyya, each with a described pattern and sound changes.
rows.anchor: جمع حاوية كزاوية وزوايا ووزنه فواعل

rows.speaker: الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Fārisī allows the plural to derive from any of the three proposed singulars, each attested; ‘or’ may also mean ‘and.’
rows.anchor: الفارسي أن يكون جمعا لكل واحد من هذه الثلاثة

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ compares the conjunction to its use in ‘Be Jews or Christians,’ for distinguishing alternatives.
rows.anchor: أبو البقاء لتفصيل مذاهبهم نظيرها في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says that when ‘or’ coordinates with fats, it expresses permissive choice, as in ‘do not obey a sinner or unbeliever.’
rows.anchor: الزجاج : هي فيما إذا كان العطف على الشحوم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains that ‘or’ makes each object independently unworthy of obedience: the phrasing prohibits obeying any one or all of them.
rows.anchor: كلهم أهل أن لايطاع فلا تطع واحدا منهم ولا تطع الجماعة

rows.speaker: العلامة الثاني
rows.claim: The Second Allāma reads ‘or’ like ‘sit with al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn’: all listed items are equally within the ruling, rather than a choice to consume some.
rows.anchor: اختاره العلامة الثاني وقال الوجه أن يقال

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭībī says attaching the three items to ‘fats’ puts all under prohibition except what was excepted; attaching them to the exception leaves only fats prohibited.
rows.anchor: وذكر الطيبي في حاصل كلام بعض المحققين في أو هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the latter construction permits eating two of the three is rejected: jurists and legal theorists recognize prohibited or permissible choices among alternatives.
rows.anchor: هذه الدعوى من العجب فان الحرام المخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That’ may refer to requital, making it an accusative cognate object, or to prohibition, making it a second object of ‘requited’; the verb takes either a prepositional or direct object.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الجزاء أو التحريم

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Mālik denies a demonstrative can refer to a verbal noun and be accusative without a following verbal noun; Abū Ḥayyān and al-Jalabī reject the restriction.
rows.anchor: ابن مالك أن اسم الاشارة لا ينتصب مشارا به إلى المصدر

rows.speaker: أبو حيان والجلبي
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān and al-Jalabī confirm a demonstrative may point to a verbal noun without a following verbal noun.
rows.anchor: أبو حيان والجلبي وصححا ورود اسم الاشارة مشارا به إلى المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses make ‘that’ the predicate of an omitted subject or a subject whose predicate omits its object pronoun.
rows.anchor: كون ذلك خبر مبتدأ مقدر أي الأمر ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wrongdoing includes killing prophets unjustly, taking usury despite its prohibition, and consuming people’s property wrongfully; each sin brought a further food prohibition.
rows.anchor: بسبب ظلمهم وهو قتلهم الانبياء بغير حق وأكلهم الربا

rows.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم
rows.claim: Another account says Israelite rulers barred the poor from birds and fats, so God prohibited those foods to them; withholding benefit may also serve a purpose or reflect earlier wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: نقل علي بن إبراهيم في تفسيره أن ملوك بني اسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is truthful in all reports, including the prohibition and its cause; some limit the reference to promise and threat.
rows.anchor: في جميع أخبارنا التي من جملتها الأخبار بالتحريم وبالبغي

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam uses the verse to support Mālik and many early authorities: only the four foods in the preceding verse are generally forbidden, and ‘claw’ means talon rather than hoof.
rows.anchor: وقوى الامام بهذه الآية ما ذهب اليه الامام مالك وكثير من السلف

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: He rejects ‘hoof’ because a hoof is hardly called a nail, and that reading would imply forbidding all hoofed animals despite the verse allowing cattle and sheep.
rows.anchor: الحافر لا يكاد يسمى ظفرا

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: He argues that the restriction applies only to Jews: the construction conveys exclusivity, and otherwise singling them out is pointless; this would leave predators and clawed birds lawful for Muslims.
rows.anchor: والآية تفيد تخصيص هذه الحرمة باليهود كما أشرنا اليه من وجهين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet forbade every fanged predator and clawed bird; the Imam calls this solitary report contrary to the Qurʾān and inadmissible.
rows.anchor: فما روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم حرم كل ذي ناب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī closes by flagging an objection to the Imam’s argument.
rows.anchor: قول الجماعة السابق وفيه نظر لا يخفى فتدبر

rows.speaker: كثير من السلف
rows.claim: Many early authorities take the command as addressed to Adam, Eve, and Iblīs; its repetition to Iblīs may show he remains bound up with humankind in earthly life.
rows.anchor: كثير من السلف أنه خطاب لآدم وحواء عليهما السلام وابليس عليه اللعنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the command may have been issued separately and summarized, as in the address to the messengers to eat good things.
rows.anchor: الأمر وقع مفرقا وهذا نقل له بالمعنى وإجمال له

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes the address to include Adam, Eve, and their descendants, thereby addressing those not yet existent.
rows.anchor: الفراء كونه خطابا لهما ولذريتهما وفيه خطاب المعدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take it to address only Adam and Eve, since the same story says ‘both of you descend’; the plural can stand for descendants because they are humanity’s source.
rows.anchor: لهما فقط لقوله سبحانه ( قال اهبطا منها جميعا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view includes Adam, Eve, Iblīs, and the serpent, with objections and answers already discussed in Sūrat al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: لهما ولابليس والحية واعترض وأجيب بما مر في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sequence has God immediately rebuke Adam for his act, without intervening event.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من النظم الكريم أن آدم عليه السلام عاجله ربه سبحانه بالعتاب

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī’s report says the forbidden tree alone caused bodily waste in Paradise, leading Adam to seek a place to relieve himself before descent; al-Ālūsī says the report is unsound.
rows.anchor: حجة الاسلام الغزالي أنه عليه السلام لما أكل من الشجرة

rows.speaker: محمد بن قيس
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Qays relates that Adam blamed Eve, she blamed the serpent, and the serpent blamed Iblīs; God assigned Eve monthly bleeding, the serpent to crawl and be struck in the face, and cursed Iblīs.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن قيس قال : إنه عليه السلام لما أكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enmity clause may be a simultaneous or prospective circumstantial clause; some grammarians take it as a new sentence answering how the descent leaves them.
rows.anchor: في موضع الحال من فاعل اهبطوا وهي حال مقارنة أو مقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enmity is straightforward if Satan is included; if only Adam and Eve are addressed, it can extend to descendants, or mean mutual oppression through Satan’s misguidance.
rows.anchor: على تقدير التخصيص بآدم وحواء عليهما السلام فقد قيل إنه باعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustaqarr means settling or a place of settlement; it may also mean earthly dominion established for them and use permitted, though that reading is less apparent.
rows.anchor: أي استقرار أو موضع استقرار فهو اما مصدر ميمي أو اسم مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word could mean a time of settlement, but that does not fit because it would repeat ‘until a time.’
rows.anchor: اسم زمان إلا أنه غير محتمل هنا لأنه يتكرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earthly enjoyment lasts until death or resurrection; dwelling in the grave may count as enjoyment in earth, and ‘for you’ may refer to humankind collectively.
rows.anchor: يريد به وقت الموت وقيل القيامة وتجعل السكنى في القبر تمتعا في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase may modify ‘enjoyment,’ both it and ‘settlement’ by attraction, or an omitted adjective clause for ‘enjoyment.’
rows.anchor: والظرف قيل متعلق بمتاع أو به وبمستقر على التنازع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed ‘He said’ marks a fresh utterance or emphasizes what follows.
rows.anchor: أعيد للاستئناف إما للايذان بعدم اتصال ما بعده بما قبله

words: فِيهَا تَحْيَوْنَ وَفِيهَا تَمُوتُونَ وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity lives and dies on earth and is brought out from it at the resurrection on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: عند البعث يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم
rows.claim: The Kūfan readers except ʿĀṣim read with fatḥa on tāʾ and ḍamma on rāʾ, as an active construction.
rows.anchor: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم ( تخرجون ) بفتح التاء وضم الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening connects to the earlier account of Sabbath transgression, showing persistence despite admonitions and warnings.
rows.anchor: عطف على إذ يعدون مسوق لبيان تماديهم في العدوان

rows.speaker: الطيبي والتفتازاني
rows.claim: Al-Ṭībī and al-Taftāzānī reject attaching it to the closer ‘when they came’: that would include the questioners among Sabbath transgressors.
rows.anchor: الطيبي والتفتازاني : ولايجوز أن يكون معطوفا على إذ تأتيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal reading makes the argument clear; the substitute reading fails because the saying followed rather than coincided with transgression, and treating the period as an extended year is strained.
rows.anchor: أن زمان القول بعد زمان العدوان ومغاير له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The group are righteous people who had not spared effort in admonishing; once they despaired of acceptance, they persisted in hope of benefit.
rows.anchor: جماعة من صلحائهم الذين لم يألوا جهدا في عظتهم حين يئسوا

words: ٱللَّهُ مُهْلِكُهُمْ أَوْ مُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Destroying them means uprooting them from earth; the alternative is severe punishment short of extermination, or destruction in this world versus punishment in the next.
rows.anchor: أي مستأصلهم بالكلية ومطهر وجه الأرض منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the world-or-afterlife reading, ‘or’ prevents exclusion, and the active participles present the outcomes as certain and virtually occurring.
rows.anchor: إيثار صيغة اسم الفاعل في الشقين للدلالة على تحقيق كل من الإهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask why rather than directly command ‘do not admonish’ because the apparent futility is astonishing, or to ask about the advice’s wisdom and benefit.
rows.anchor: مبالغة في أن الوعظ لاينجع فيهم إذ المقصود لاتعظوا أو أتعظون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question may have been an exchange among righteous preachers, one asking why they continued an ineffectual task.
rows.anchor: هذا تقاول وقع بين الصلحاء الواعظين كأنه قال بعضهم لبعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either group of questioners may have spoken in the sinners’ presence to encourage repentance, since a firm prediction of doom may instill fear.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل على كلا القولين أن ذلك صدر من القائل بمحصر من القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view makes the Sabbath violators the speakers, mocking the warners, but the commentator considers this unlikely.
rows.anchor: قائلو ذلك المعتدون في السبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘As an excuse’ may be a purpose complement to admonishing, an absolute object after an omitted verb, or an object of ‘they said’ denoting apology.
rows.anchor: نعظهم معذرة إليه تعالى على أنه مفعول له

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Maʿdhira originally means excuse or clearing oneself from sin; al-Azharī glosses it as apology, and ‘to’ reflects conveying it to God.
rows.anchor: وقال الأزهري : إنه بمعنى الاعتذار وعداه بإلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God ‘your Lord’ indirectly rebukes the questioners; on the literal reading, the reply wisely redirects from the expected answer.
rows.anchor: إضافة الرب إلى ضمير المخاطبين نوع تعريض بالسائلين

rows.speaker: من عدا حفص والمفضل
rows.claim: All readers except Ḥafṣ and al-Mufaḍḍal read the word in the nominative as predicate of an omitted subject: ‘our admonition is an excuse.’
rows.anchor: من عدا حفص والمفضل ( معذرة ) بالرفع على أنه خبر مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause coordinates with ‘as an excuse,’ expressing hope that they attain at least some piety.
rows.anchor: عطف على معذرة أي ورجاء أن يتقوا بعض التقاة

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: Shaykh al-Islām says the wording explicitly shows the questioners are not part of the doomed group.
rows.anchor: شيخ الإسلام : وهذا صريح في أن القائلين لم تعظون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To preserve the view that questioners were Sabbath violators, one may posit a shift in address or wording patterned on their calling themselves ‘a people’; both depart from the apparent sense.
rows.anchor: القول بأنه إلتفات أو مشاكلة لتعبيرهم عن أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘They forgot’ means they abandoned what the righteous reminded them of and turned away completely; the relative pronoun is apparent, though a verbal noun is possible.
rows.anchor: تركوا ما ذكرهم به صلحاؤهم ترك الناسي للشيء وأعرضوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetfulness figuratively denotes abandonment, preferably as a metaphor comparing disregard with forgetting; a metonymy based on causation is also possible.
rows.anchor: والنسيان مجاز عن الترك واستظهر أنه إستعارة حيث شبه الترك بالنسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Literal forgetfulness is not intended: it does not incur punishment, and salvation follows deliberate abandonment; the condition implies reminders and refusal to heed them.
rows.anchor: ولم يحمل ظاهره كما قال بعض المحققين لأنه غير واقع ولأنه لايؤاخذ بالنسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those forbidding evil includes both questioners and addressed people; the questioners also admonished but stopped when they concluded it would have no effect.
rows.anchor: شامل للذين قالوا لم تعظون الخ وللمقول لهم ذلك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says one who knows admonition will not affect the listener is relieved of the duty and may have to stop lest it become pointless; he compares warning extortionists robbing the poor.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري لدخوله في باب العبث ألا ترى أنك لو ذهبت إلى المكاسين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first group may have stopped from greater certainty that warnings were futile, while the others were less despairing or exceptionally eager and persistent.
rows.anchor: كما وصف الله تعالى رسوله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās said he did not know what became of the silent faction, since the verse saves warners and punishes wrongdoers without naming the silent.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima argued that the silent had condemned the wrong, so even though God did not explicitly say He saved them, He did not say He destroyed them; Ibn ʿAbbās was pleased and concluded they were saved.
rows.anchor: عكرمة : جعلني الله فداك ألا تراهم كيف أنكروا

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī attributes to Ibn ʿAbbās two other positions: suspend judgment on the silent, or hold they were destroyed; the latter also is attributed to Ibn Zayd and Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
rows.anchor: الطبرسي إليه رضي الله تعالى عنه قولين آخرين في الساكتة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses baʾīs as punishment without mercy, amounting to severity; most treat the form as adjective or emphatic verbal noun used adjectivally.
rows.anchor: وفسره الحبر بما لا رحمة فيه ويرجع إلى ما ذكر

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says buʾs, baʾs, and baʾsāʾ mean hardship and adversity; buʾs is especially poverty and war, while baʾs and baʾsāʾ denote punitive calamity.
rows.anchor: الراغب : البؤس والبأس والبأساء الشدة والمكروه

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr reads biʾays on the fayʿil pattern, comparable to ḍaygham; adding yāʾ to a verbal noun can make a noun or adjective.
rows.anchor: أبوبكر ( بيئس ) على فيعل كضيغم

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: A narration from ʿĀṣim has the hamza kasra; al-Ālūsī calls it weak in transmission and grammar, softened by the affinity of hamzated and weak forms.
rows.anchor: عاصم في رواية عنه ( بيئس ) بكسر الهمزة إنها ضعيفة

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads biʾis with kasra on bāʾ and sukūn on hamza, explained as a shortened form like kabid/kibd and kalima/kilma.
rows.anchor: ابن عامر ( بئس ) بكسر الباء وسكون الهمزة

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads bīs, turning hamza into yāʾ after sukūn and preceding kasra; another analysis derives it from biʾsa, ‘to blame,’ converted to a noun for loathsome punishment.
rows.anchor: نافع ( بيس ) على قلب الهمزة ياء كما قلبت في ذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another bīs reading assimilates the hamza-derived yāʾ, or derives from a wāw-root; further forms include lightened bīs and bāʾis meaning one possessing strength.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( بيس ) كريس وكيس على قلب الهمزة ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings are reported, with some authorities counting as many as twenty-six variants.
rows.anchor: وقريء غير ذلك وأوصل بعضهم ما فيه من القراءات إلى ست وعشرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite ‘punishment’ intensifies its magnitude and horror.
rows.anchor: وتنكير العذاب للتفخيم والتهويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final causal phrase attaches to ‘We seized,’ as does the earlier cause, without awkwardness because meanings differ; wrongdoing causes seizure and itself constitutes further injustice.
rows.anchor: متعلق بأخذنا كالباء الأولى ولا ضير فيه لاختلافهما معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successors came after the people just mentioned, or after the righteous predecessors.
rows.anchor: أي المذكورين وقيل : الصالحين ( خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalaf with open lām means a bad successor, a verbal noun used adjectivally or a collective noun, and commonly denotes evil; an Arabic saying illustrates it.
rows.anchor: أي بدل سوء مصدر نعت به ولذلك يقع على الواحد والجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalf with sukūn on lām is often used for a good successor; some say it is specifically positive, while others treat the forms as synonymous for any successor.
rows.anchor: والخلف بفتح اللام في الخير

rows.speaker: حسان
rows.claim: Ḥassān’s verse uses khalf in praise of successors who follow in obedience to God.
rows.anchor: حسان : لنا القدم الأولى إليك وخلفنا لا ولنا في طاعة الله تابع

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labīd’s verse uses khalaf in blame for the wretched company that remained.
rows.anchor: لبيد : ذهب الذين يعاش في أكنافهم وبقيت في خلف كجلد الأجرب

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrans allow both vocalizations for bad successors but only open-lām for good ones; most linguists agree, except al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayda.
rows.anchor: عن البصريين أنه يجوز التحريك والسكون في الردى وأما الجيد فبالتحريك فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word may derive from succession or corruption and change, as in the altered breath of a fasting person.
rows.anchor: اشتقاقه إما من الخلافة أو من الخلوف وهو الفساد والتغيير

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abū Ḥātim says khalf with sukūn means offspring, singular and plural alike, while khalaf with fatḥa is replacement, child or stranger.
rows.anchor: أبو حاتم : الخلف بالسكون الأولاد الواحد والجمع فيه سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most identify the successors as contemporaries of the Prophet; they are apparently Jews, since they cannot be believers in him.
rows.anchor: الأكثرون على أن المراد بهؤلاء الخلف الذين كانوا في عصر رسول الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies the successors as Christians, a view al-Ālūsī considers unsound.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد أنهم النصارى وليس بذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book is the Torah; inheritance is figurative because successors possessed it and knew its contents after forebears.
rows.anchor: أي التوراة والوراثة مجاز عن كونها في أيديهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads the verb as passive, with ḍamma and shadda.
rows.anchor: الحسن ( ورثوا ) بالضم والتشديد مبنيا لما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may independently describe what they did with the book after inheriting it; Abū al-Baqāʾ and others parse it as circumstantial to ‘they inherited.’
rows.anchor: إستئناف مسوق لبيان ما يصنعون بالكتاب بعد وراثتهم إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAraḍ denotes transient property and worldly chattels; theologians borrowed it for an accident as opposed to substance.
rows.anchor: والعرض مالا ثبات له ومنه إستعار المتكلمون العرض لمقابل الجوهر

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda uses the vowelled form for worldly goods other than gold and silver, and the unvowelled form for money and value.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيدة : هو غير النقدين من متاعها وبالسكون المال والقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-adnā modifies an omitted ‘thing’ and means worldly life near relative to the afterlife, rather than the less likely sense ‘lowly.’
rows.anchor: ( الأدنى ) صفة لمحذوف أي الشيء الأدنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly gain refers specifically to bribes in judgments and taking payment for distorting scripture.
rows.anchor: المراد بهذا العرض ما يأخذونه من الرشا في الحكومات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They claim God will pardon and overlook their sin; this clause coordinates with what precedes rather than being circumstantial.
rows.anchor: ولا يؤاخذنا الله تعالى بذلك ويتجاوز عنا والجملة عطف على ما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive verb may be construed with the prepositional phrase as complement, or with an implicit pronoun referring to them.
rows.anchor: والفعل مسند إلى الجار والمجرور وجوز أن يكون مسندا إلى ضمير يأخذون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause may be circumstantial to ‘they say,’ understood as belief: they claim forgiveness while persisting in and repeating the same sin without repentance.
rows.anchor: في موضع الحال قيل من ضمير يقولون والقول بمعنى الاعتقاد
